name: LOW POINTS
clue: Badwater Basin, 282 feet below sea level, lies in this national park, just 85 miles from the tallest peak in the lower 48

name: CORPS VALUES
clue: Jefferson sent this pair and their Corps of Discovery to explore the Louisiana Purchase; they reached the Pacific in 1805

name: BOXED IN
clue: Hesiod's first mortal woman, she unsealed a jar, not a box, loosing every ill on mankind but leaving hope inside

name: LANDLOCKED
clue: This South American nation lost its coast to Chile in the 1880s yet still keeps a navy, which trains on Lake Titicaca

name: EPIC TITLES
clue: Homer's epic of the Trojan War is titled not for its hero Achilles but for this alternate name for Troy

name: WORTH ITS WEIGHT
clue: It takes roughly 150 crocus flowers, each plucked by hand, to yield a single gram of the world's costliest spice

name: FINAL EPISODES
clue: Over 100 million Americans watched 'Goodbye, Farewell and Amen,' the 1983 finale of this sitcom set in the Korean War

name: BROADWAY RECORDS
clue: Opened in 1988, this Andrew Lloyd Webber musical had run 13,981 performances, more than any Broadway show, when it closed in 2023

name: SUE-PERSTAR
clue: Named for the fossil hunter who found her in South Dakota in 1990, Sue is the Field Museum's $8.36 million example of this species

name: ORGAN RECITAL
clue: Prometheus' punishment made grim sense: this organ can regrow to full size from as little as a quarter of itself

name: THE MATH BEHIND PHYSICS
clue: Einstein eulogized this German as a 'creative mathematical genius'; her theorem ties each symmetry of nature to a conservation law

name: GOING THE DISTANCE
clue: Its odd 26-mile-385-yard length dates to the 1908 London Olympics, where the route ran from Windsor Castle to the royal box

name: IT'S ALL GREEK TO HER
clue: Egypt's last active pharaoh, she was a Macedonian Greek, reputedly the first in her 275-year dynasty to learn Egyptian

name: AND THE OSCAR GOES TO...
clue: Dustin Hoffman's 'I'm walkin' here!' comes from this 1969 tale of 2 New York hustlers, the only X-rated Best Picture winner

name: LANGUAGE ISOLATES
clue: Spoken on both sides of the Pyrenees, this European tongue has no known relatives and predates the arrival of Indo-European

name: MOLD RUSH
clue: Returning from vacation in 1928, Alexander Fleming found a stray mold killing his staph colonies, the source of this drug

name: FACE THE MUSIC
clue: Deaf by the 1824 premiere of his Ninth Symphony, this composer had to be turned around by a singer to see the applause

name: CELL BIOLOGY
clue: These organelles carry their own DNA, inherited only from your mother, a legacy of the free-living bacteria they once were

name: A BRUSH WITH HISTORY
clue: Jacques-Louis David painted this radical journalist dead in his medicinal bath, where Charlotte Corday stabbed him in 1793

name: DRINK TO THAT
clue: Its tune began as a London drinking club's 'To Anacreon in Heaven,' and Congress didn't make it official until 1931

name: LIGHT THE WAY
clue: Celebrating Rama's return to Ayodhya, this five-day autumn 'festival of lights' fills India with oil lamps and fireworks

name: THE CONSTITUTION
clue: It's the only addition to the Constitution ratified to undo an earlier one, ending a 13-year 'noble experiment'

name: PROOF POSITIVE
clue: In 1931 this Austrian logician proved that any consistent system of arithmetic contains truths it can never prove

name: LINES OF LATITUDE
clue: Its monument to the line that gives it its name, built near its capital before GPS, stands some 240 meters off the real thing

name: SIEGE THE DAY
clue: Homer's Iliad never mentions this hollow ruse, and it's Virgil's Aeneid that tells the famous story of how it ended a 10-year war

name: CEILING THE DEAL
clue: Insisting he was a sculptor, not a painter, this creator of 'David' spent 4 years frescoing a chapel ceiling for Pope Julius II

name: DYING DECLARATIONS
clue: These rivals turned pen pals died hours apart on July 4, 1826, one's last words wrongly noting that the other 'survives'

name: STELLAR NEIGHBORS
clue: Its name means 'nearest,' and this red dwarf, about 4.2 light-years away, is the closest star to our sun

name: WAR PAINT
clue: He asked that his stark mural of a 1937 town bombing stay at New York's MoMA until democracy returned to Spain, as it did in 1981

name: SCHOOL TIES
clue: Shakespeare enrolled this brooding prince at Wittenberg, the same university town where Luther posted his 95 theses
